solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Most ill-tempered priests opt to reform (10)

indicatorNotes.reform: to reform is to form again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A grumpy bunch of clergy choose to mend their ways.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pairs bad-tempered priests with reform, so 'reform' reads as moral improvement; here it only rebuilds the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Stroppy is British slang for bad-tempered and awkward, and this is its superlative.

entries.clue: Son with stringed instrument is keen (5)

indicatorNotes.with: with means alongside, so the two pieces sit next to each other

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
a stringed instrument plucked by hand

annotation.surface: A young musician is enthusiastic about his harp.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like enthusiasm in the surface, but it is used in its other sense, as a keen blade.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the cutting sense: a keen blade has a fine edge.

entries.clue: Earnest talks to resettle venomous reptiles (12)

indicatorNotes.to resettle: resettling moves things to new places, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Serious negotiations are held about moving dangerous snakes to a new home.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a wildlife-relocation meeting, which hides that 'Earnest talks' is just a pile of letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: these American pit vipers, named for the rattle on the tail, are venomous reptiles.

entries.clue: Father on church step (4)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, A on B puts A above B

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
CE = Church of England

annotation.surface: A priest stands on the church step.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Father' suggests a priest, and a church step suggests a stair; both turn out to be something else.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a single stride taken in walking.

entries.clue: Leader abandoning African land for European peninsula (6)

indicatorNotes.abandoning: the leader abandons the word, so its first letter goes

blocks.note: Liberia, the West African country, loses its first letter, L

annotation.surface: A head of state flees an African country for Spain or Portugal.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface paints a ruler in exile; 'Leader' is only the first letter of the country.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain name: the peninsula shared by Spain and Portugal in south-west Europe.

entries.clue: Wealth that woman had — love received by boy (8)

indicatorNotes.received by: the boy receives love, taking it inside him

blocks.note: she'd is short for she had; the apostrophe is ignored
a lad is a boy
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

annotation.surface: She was rich, and her love was returned by a young man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'That woman had' is a contraction in disguise: she'd. The definition is loose, since a shedload is a large amount of anything, here of money.
annotation.definitionFit: A British slang sense: a great quantity, so a vast sum of money counts as wealth.

entries.clue: Difficult to take responsibility for part of motorway (4,8)

blocks.note: hard = difficult
to shoulder a burden is to take responsibility for it

annotation.surface: It is tough to be blamed for a bit of the motorway.
annotation.walkthrough: A motorway is a British highway; 'for' links wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A British road term: the paved strip at the edge of a motorway where broken-down vehicles stop.

entries.clue: Rest on ship, welcoming cruise on vacation (6)

indicatorNotes.welcoming: the ship welcomes the cruise letters inside it
indicatorNotes.on vacation: vacated, the word is emptied, keeping only its outer letters

blocks.note: re = on, concerning
SS = steamship
CRUISE emptied of its middle leaves C…E

annotation.surface: Taking a break aboard a liner, enjoying a holiday cruise.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all holiday, which is what hides 'on vacation' as an emptying instruction rather than time off.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a break from work, as when parliament or a school stops for a time.

entries.clue: Maybe a newspaper piece (7)

blocks.note: 'a' is a grammatical word class member, and 'maybe' flags it as one example
a written item in a newspaper

annotation.walkthrough: 'Maybe a' reads as filler, but it is a definition by example: 'a' is the indefinite article, and 'maybe' marks it as one instance.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: in grammar 'a', 'an' and 'the' belong to this word class, and a written newspaper item goes by the same name.

entries.clue: Wipe out facility housing Resistance (5)

indicatorNotes.housing: one thing houses another by holding it inside

blocks.note: facility = ease, as in doing something with facility
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

annotation.surface: Destroy a building that sheltered the Resistance fighters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Facility' suggests a building, but it means ease of doing something; 'Resistance' looks like a wartime movement and is just R.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to rub out or delete, as with a pencil mark or a file.

entries.clue: Hide exposed spy, English lieutenant (4)

indicatorNotes.exposed: exposed means stripped of its covering, so the word loses its outer letters

blocks.note: SPY without its outer letters leaves P
E = English
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

annotation.surface: An English officer, unmasked as a spy, has to go into hiding.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hide' reads as a verb in the surface, but the answer is the noun: an animal's skin.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the noun sense: an animal's skin with its fur on.

entries.clue: Remove leads from dogs in Swiss cabin (8)

indicatorNotes.leads from: the leads are the leading letters of the following words

blocks.note: first letters of dogs, in, Swiss
a lodge is a small cabin, often in the mountains

annotation.surface: Take the dogs off their leashes inside an Alpine chalet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leads' looks like dog leashes, and 'Swiss cabin' like a single unit; the leads are first letters, and 'Swiss' supplies one of them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to shift something from where it is fixed, as a stone from a wall.

entries.clue: Come down from cedar and see ground (8)

indicatorNotes.ground: ground as in crushed to bits, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Climb down from the cedar tree and look at the ground below.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ground' reads as the earth under the tree; it is the past tense of grind.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: prices or numbers come down when they fall.

entries.clue: Liking sculpture primarily in gallery (5)

indicatorNotes.primarily: primarily means first of all, so take the first letter
indicatorNotes.in: one piece goes in the other

blocks.note: the Tate is a group of London art galleries
first letter of sculpture

annotation.surface: Someone is fond of the statues in an art gallery.
annotation.walkthrough: The Tate is the national art gallery group in London, a common crossword gallery.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a liking for jazz is a fondness or preference for it.

entries.clue: Vacated tiny company, working for business magnate (6)

indicatorNotes.Vacated: a vacated word is emptied, keeping only its outer letters

blocks.note: TINY emptied leaves T…Y
Co = company
on = working, as a machine that is on

annotation.surface: A small firm moves out of its premises and goes to work for a tycoon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vacated' reads as a firm moving out; it empties 'tiny'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from a Japanese title for a shogun, now used of any rich industrialist.

entries.clue: Musketeer beat hostile guards (5)

indicatorNotes.guards: the phrase guards the answer, holding it inside

blocks.note: the letters straddle the gap: the last two of the first word and the first three of the second

annotation.surface: A swordsman defeats enemy sentries.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Guards' looks like a noun, the soldiers being beaten; it is a verb telling you the answer is held inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of the three heroes of Dumas's The Three Musketeers.

entries.clue: State why Gawain hid away from all outsiders (6)

indicatorNotes.away from all outsiders: every word is taken away from its outer letters, leaving only the insides

blocks.note: WHY without its outer letters
GAWAIN without its outer letters
HID without its outer letters

annotation.surface: Explain why the Arthurian knight Gawain kept away from strangers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hid' looks like part of the story, but it is the third word being stripped; 'State' is a US state, not the verb to say.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Pacific island group is one of the fifty US states.

entries.clue: President locks spy chief in prison (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the pieces go in the prison

blocks.note: locks of hair
M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories
the can is slang for prison

annotation.surface: The head of state locks up his intelligence chief.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Locks' reads as a verb for imprisoning, but it is a noun: hair.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the person presiding over a board, society or meeting.

entries.clue: Section of fences supporting turning cat (4)

indicatorNotes.Section of: a section is a piece cut from the phrase

blocks.note: the letters straddle the gap between the two words; turning then reverses them

annotation.surface: A stretch of fence holds up a cat as it spins round.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supporting' looks like the fences are propping something up; it only supplies letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A familiar, affectionate word for a cat, as when calling one in.

entries.clue: Give letters of enchantment (5)

blocks.note: to name the letters of a word in order
a magic charm or bewitchment

annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, the letters of a magic word, but splits into two meanings.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: naming a word's letters in order, and a magic charm cast on someone.

entries.clue: Unclothed parts of legs reaching far up (4)

indicatorNotes.Unclothed: unclothed means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters go

blocks.note: THIGHS, the upper parts of the legs, stripped of their outer letters

annotation.surface: Bare thighs on show, the skirt riding up.
annotation.walkthrough: Unlike most clues of this kind, the word to strip is not printed; you find THIGHS from 'parts of legs' first.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something a long way up, as a shelf out of reach or a bird in the sky.

entries.clue: Ring great Greek character (5)

blocks.note: a ring is round, like the letter O
mega = great, as in slang

annotation.surface: Calling up a splendid Greek personality.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person, but here it is a letter of the alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the last letter of the Greek alphabet.

entries.clue: Fabulous girl regularly dances on air (7)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take letters at regular intervals, every other one
indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, A on B puts A after B

blocks.note: an aria is an air, a song in opera
taken regularly, every other letter: D, N, E

annotation.surface: A wonderful young woman dances as if floating.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means from fable here, not wonderful: the answer is from Greek myth. 'Air' means a tune.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the princess of Greek myth who gave Theseus the thread to escape the labyrinth.

entries.clue: Help repair broken device connected to computer (10)

indicatorNotes.broken: broken into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Someone asks for help fixing a faulty computer gadget.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface is an IT support request, so 'broken' reads as faulty rather than as an instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: printers, mice and keyboards are all devices plugged into a computer.
